I am playing Monopoly as an AI player.

I have $366 and four unmortgaged properties. I am analyzing the board to decide whether to trade or mortgage.

p2 owns Boardwalk and most of the green and yellow groups. p3 owns Park Place and most of the red and pink groups. The bank has 32 houses and 12 hotels. Several properties remain unowned.

I will keep all four properties and avoid trading or mortgaging. I have enough cash to buy Kentucky or Atlantic if needed. I am now deciding whether to trade, mortgage, or end my turn.

I am verifying which color groups are actually at risk of monopolies. p3 only owns one red property, so no red monopoly exists yet. p3 owns two pinks, so States blocks a potential pink monopoly.

p1 controls two-thirds of the orange, light blue, and yellow groups. p2 controls two-thirds of the green group. p3 controls two-thirds of the pink group. My New York Avenue blocks p1's orange monopoly. Indiana Avenue blocks a potential red monopoly.

I considered trading for monopolies but found no profitable deals. p1 would demand New York Avenue in exchange for St James and Tennessee, which is a net loss. p3 would demand Indiana Avenue for St Charles and Virginia, which is also unprofitable. I could buy Atlantic Avenue from the bank to complete the yellow group.

I can afford Baltic, Oriental, Kentucky, and Atlantic with my $366. Pennsylvania Avenue is too expensive. I will end my turn.

I rejected a trade offer from p1 for New York Avenue. They offered $400 plus Short Line and Electric, but I now see that even a higher price would be suicide. With $1120 in cash, they could immediately build three houses on New York Avenue and collect $750 in rent, or a hotel for $1000. I will not trade away my orange blocker.
